Content: Fuling... are you feeling all right now?
Mhm, don't worry about me. The new medicine is actually working really well. I feel surprisingly energetic now!
That's a relief... Kuiren mentioned that anyone who watches the Carriage Procession will be blessed with good fortune.
Just let me know if you get tired, okay? I can carry you back.
I-I'm fine, really... The doctor said I need to walk and stretch my legs anyway—Ah... look over there, Wuli! Isn't that beautiful?
Mm. Very beautiful indeed.
Mmh... this is incredible! Seriously, you have to try it—Blegh!
Are you serious? You're literally throwing up! And tears are streaming down your face!
I just choked! Come on, I'd never lie to you! This is good stuff, I swear!
Really? Well, just one bite then... Blegh!
Ahahaha—Blegh!
You little—Blegh!
Stop talking—Blegh!
Oh, no... I spent all my pocket money. I'm so gonna get it this time...
What did you buy?
A Moon Fox lantern, two <ano=candied fruit>Tanghulu</ano> skewers, and a pack of Moonlight Sparklers...
I gave the lantern to Yishu, and the Tanghulu... I bought them for Mom and Dad, but they were so tasty I ate them...
I promised Mom I'd save my money... What if I say a big gust of wind blew the money away? Do you think she'd believe me?
Probably not...
Maybe you should just tell her the truth.
Ugh...
I can't... Mom's got a short fuse...
Zhumei! Th-there's something I've wanted to tell you for a long time! I, uh... well...
Hm? What is it?
I mean... you... you look... really pretty today.
...Oh, thank you. You look quite sharp yourself, Maqing.
So... was there anything else you wanted to tell me?
Oh! Yes! I, uh... I've always...
You've always...?
Always... wanted to take you out to dinner at Yuan's Flavors!
Mm-hmm... That sounds lovely.
Sir, the storyteller's legends are so different from what's written in our history books...
Say, if Paragon Qingxiao and Sentinel Hsin the Moon Fox actually went all out, who do you think would win?
Is that even a question? Lady Hsin is a Sentinel. Who in this world is more powerful than a Sentinel?
But I heard Paragon Qingxiao can summon countless swords hundreds of meters tall! I'd say she's got a fighting chance.
Oh yeah? Lady Hsin can conjure an entire city out of thin air and drop it right on her head. Boom.
But then the Paragon could summon a vast formation of giant swords and channel her Sword Intent into an impenetrable shield!
...Then Lady Hsin could just turn all of Xuanfang Hold into one giant Autopuppet that swallows the Paragon whole, swords and all!
...Sure, but then the Paragon would make her swords go wild inside its belly and cut her way out from the inside!
Then... then Lady Hsin would just conjure another city!
Would there even be a Land of Xuanfang left after all that...
Mhm... This year's Waking Moon Brew... is so good...
Zzz... Zzz...
It's a quiet Autopuppet, but somehow, you feel like it's observing you.
(Get close to study it.)
I see what you're doing here.
The Autopuppet stays put.
(Stare at it.)
(Leave.)
Uh... please don't tell anyone...
This voice... Are you Leyue?
I knew it...
Ahaha... you really are sharp.
It's good to see you again. Yes, it's me—Leyue.
You vanished right in front of me last time. I thought you were...
"I am Sentinel Hsin the Moon Fox. A sudden crisis has struck the Sanctum, leaving me trapped in its deepest depths..."
"You have been chosen to assist me in reclaiming Xuanfang Hold. As my next Resonator, you must..."
...Send 80,000 Shell Credits to rebuild the Celestial Ring Formation? Wait, this is obviously a scam! Tell me you didn't actually send them money!
Uh, no... I-I didn't...
By the way... do you mind buying me lunch today? I'm... a little strapped for cash lately.

Legend has it that the Ministry of Development once had a prodigy on their hands. One with the rare talent to command the mountains and oceans. She even built the entire Bird-Return Garden in a single night!
Impressive! And then what happened?
She just vanished into thin air one day...
Left nothing behind but a tuft of tail fur on the blueprints. That's when it hit them... she was Hsin the Moon Fox in disguise, come to help the Artisans crack what they couldn't!
Yeah, yeah, keep making things up. She's a Sentinel! Hsin the Moon Fox doesn't shed.
The Waking Moon Festival is finally here... When will Lady Sentinel arrive?
Grandma... Hsin the Moon Fox isn't coming. Just try not to think about it.
You always said She'd come, but She never shows. Those old legends are just made-up stories.
It's different this time. She will be here.
Someone saw Her walking down from the Sanctum alongside that great hero who saved Jinzhou!
Everything is going to get better... for all of Xuanfang.
...Xuanfang's been doing just fine on its own, even with Hsin the Moon Fox gone!
I'm gonna see what this long-lost Sentinel looks like for myself...
I heard the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs has sent someone to the Land of Xuanfang... Think you might know a thing or two about it?
Of course I do! They say that Intendant is no small figure, plus she's got history with Lady Hsin...

She dresses all in black, is always seen with an umbrella, and comes and goes without a trace. A mystery through and through, and worth ten of any other. Wherever she passes, folks can't help but stare...
...You're not just making this up?
That's just the word on the street.
First time at the Waking Moon Festival? Well, well, you've found the perfect guide!

For daytime, I'd say the Carriage Procession and a taste of Waking Moon Brew are a must. And by night? Go watch the fish lantern dances and make a wish with the Water Moon Lanterns. Trust me, it's a sight you won't want to miss!
So, how about it? Need a local guide? Honest prices, satisfaction guaranteed. I can even wait in line for you at Yuan's Flavors!
...No need? That's quite alright! Then how about these Xuanfang mechanism models? The craftsmanship is exquisite. They make perfect souvenirs!
Care for a look? Only 500 Shell Credits!
Alright, everyone! Today I'm gonna show you the must-try dishes at the Waking Moon Festival!
First up: Cloudward Stew. Savory, packed with flavor... Mmm, this is sooo good!
Next on the list: Stir-Fried Trio. Spicy, savory, perfect with rice. Yum yum!
Now for Mengzhou's No. 1 pastry: Moon Fox Rice Cake. Say less, people. This one's a solid ten out of ten!
Alright, now I'm taking you to try the signature dish at Yuan's Flavors. Stay tuned!
N-no way... The fourth and fifth volumes of "Meteorite Tiger Blade"?!
Hehe. A friend from Jinzhou came in for the Waking Moon Festival and brought them along by chance. I knew you were dying to read them, so I kept them right here just for you.
I can't believe my wish on the Moon Lantern came true so fast... Thank you SOOO much!
Don't gobble the Water Moon Cakes straight from the steamer. While they're still hot, add a scoop of ice cream and a drizzle of plum sauce...
You'll get a cool, creamy richness on the first bite, followed by the warm, pillowy cake. You'll enjoy that lovely contrast while the plum's tart bite cuts through the sweetness...
Just try it. One bite, and you'll be too busy enjoying it to talk.
You must be a true gourmet... Now I've gotta try one too!

[Xianling Village Farmhouse] Grand Opening Special: half-price on everything! Be the first to taste our Waking Moon Feast. Even the Golden-Eyed One swears by it!
Reply "Unsub" to unsubscribe.
But I haven't tried it yet.
Unsub.
But I haven't tried it yet.
Shoot, did this actually go to {PlayerName}'s Terminal...?
Unsub.
Don't go, valued patron! This text reaching you must be fate. Come give us a try! You won't regret it!
[Auto-reply] We'd love to have you here!
(First the Autopuppets going rogue, then the grim omen from the Providence Lock, and now the Intendant coming in person.)
(No matter what happens to Xuanfang Hold... I will keep them safe, whatever it takes.)
You must be Tangning. Intendant Suoming is expecting you.
You must be Tangning. Intendant Suoming is expecting you.
I am Jiqing. Thank you for your service. Ten years in the Hold is no small thing.
It's nothing. But may I ask, do you have any insight into what she might be thinking?
What she's thinking? Meaning?
I don't doubt the Intendant's competence. I'm sure she can handle whatever comes.
But... she doesn't feel for Xuanfang Hold the way I do. And those rumors about her, two hundred years back...
I'm afraid she'll sacrifice the Hold's best interests for the Ministry's ends.
Seems you're not very familiar with those rumors, or else I doubt you'd think that.
I know that everyone who fought beside her back then were all—
Easy now. Speak with Intendant Suoming yourself. If you have concerns, voice them directly.
(If the Intendant truly means to leave the Hold to its fate, then I'll have to...)
Intendant Suoming.
Yes. Speak.
Not long ago, my Providence Lock opened on its own. Following its guidance, I went in secret to the Manifold Sanctum and measured the Sentinel's frequency.
There's no mistaking it. Her frequency is fading fast. I fear the Sanctum could fall at any moment.
I see. Your years of reporting to the Ministry on all that has occurred here are duly noted.
All of it, exactly as you foresaw a century ago.
I understand your final charge. I will deliver it into "Hsin's" hands.
Forgive me. In the end, the promise went unkept.
No matter. From the day we met, I have known you gave everything you had.
And the promise is only deferred. A hundred years is nothing. Without you in Mengzhou, the Ministry will have much to do.
Then it all falls to you, Suoming.
You needn't say that. This was all part of your design, wasn't it?
Not design. Only faith. Faith in you... and in Her.
Today's the day, then...
The Manifold Sanctum and Hsin the Moon Fox are one and the same. I must see the truth for myself before it falls.
Only the three of us will go, lest we rouse the "snake." We should not draw attention.
But—
Say, on this trip to the village, we're not having that same stuff again, are we?
...Mengzhou Fish in Vinegar?
Eugh, yeah. Besides that, Xuanfang's full of good eats. Brocade Pearl Meatballs, Stir-Fried Trio, Jade Mushroom Soup... Slurrrp! Aww, now my tummy's rumbling again...
Abby, your appetite is always right on cue.
Heheh. C'mon, let's go grab a meal!
Come one, come all! You won't regret—Oh! {PlayerName}, is that you?! Welcome, welcome!
Our farmhouse restaurant is finally open for business! Here to sample the new menu?
Your spam ad blew up my Terminal...
I'm here for that Waking Moon Feast even the Golden-Eyed One swears by.
Wha—? Ah, well... haha, sorry about that! Today's meal is on us, so try anything you like!
Ha, you're a funny one! Ahaha...
My honest apologies! We just thought it sounded catchier that way. Your meal today's on us, so try anything you like!
What would you recommend?
That'd be our new Moon Fox Rice Cakes, no question. They're Lady Hsin's favorite treat!
So you're really set on moving to Mengzhou?
Of course! Once the Censure Courts clear out the last of the Tacet Discords, Xuanfang Hold will have served its purpose and collapse. We've known that since day one, haven't we?
It can't just crumble overnight, though. The Ministry of War would give notice first, wouldn't they?
Oh, please... Think about all the strange things that've been happening. Sit around waiting for an official notice, and you'll be caught with your trousers down.
And with the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs sending people now... something big's brewing. You can count on it...
Anyway, better to be ahead of the curve than buried under it. When things go sideways, who knows what else might happen...
That's... kind of jumping at shadows, isn't it?
Ugh, you never see past your own nose. Forget it. Eat up, eat up.
(Xuanfang Hold collapsing... at a time like this? And the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs...)
(I remember their reach extends all across Huanglong... If they're showing up now, it must involve Hsin in some way.)
(Oh... ran straight into {Male=him;Female=her} the second I stepped out.)
(Given my position, I really ought to speak with {Male=him;Female=her}, but—)
(Better see Intendant Suoming first. Safer to let her decide how to approach the Arbiter.)

At a tea stall, you overhear patrons trading hushed rumors that Xuanfang Hold is on the verge of collapse. They note that the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs has sent people into the Land of Xuanfang, surely a sign that something big is brewing. You suspect they must be here for Hsin the Moon Fox.
 
Unnoticed behind you, Tangning of the Ministry passes by, heading to report to Intendant Suoming.
(Last time I saw Intendant Suoming, I was still a fresh recruit.)
(Ten years, gone in a blink...)
Tangning? Well, look at you. All dressed up.
Tangning? Well, look at you. All dressed up.
Dressed up? Feels like a plain old work uniform to me.
You? Work? I only ever see you loafing about the Hold, teasing birds, sipping tea, gabbing with anyone who listen.
Ouch. You make me sound useless... even if you're not wrong. Anyway, I'm off. Gotta go see the boss.
To be honest, I'm a little nervous. Heard she once ousted the local officials back home and took over herself...
Is this job of yours above board? Sounds like you work for a tyrant.
I just worry we won't see eye to eye. That what matters to me... might mean nothing to her.
What's with the doom and gloom? You'll be fine, I know it.
Remember that rogue Autopuppet that smashed into my house? You took it down with a yawn while fixing your hair.
I had no idea I was that good. And are you telling me to pick a fight with her...?
Haha. Tell you what, I just made some Moon Fox Rice Cakes. Bring them along as a gift for your scary boss.
Oh... thank you.
(I heard Intendant Suoming dislikes anything bitter-tasting. These rice cakes might just be...)
Tangning...
Up and about already, Yao?
Mm. I'm much better now.
Aw! You've been working hard, haven't you? For that, half these rice cakes are yours!
Go easy on them, though. You just got better.
Thanks... Tangning, what's that thing on your waist?
This? It's called the <te href=852011>Providence Lock</te>. A gift from the Sentinel.
From the Sentinel? Really?
Mm-hm. When I'm in trouble, it opens and helps me. Want it?
No thanks. Whenever I'm stuck, big brother Tangning always comes to help me.
You've helped me so, so many times already!
Aww. You're too sweet, Yao. Now I feel like giving you all the rice cakes...
But you're right! If you or anyone else might be in danger, I can't afford to freeze up. Not even in front of Intendant Suoming.
Mm... I don't really understand. But please don't get hurt, Tangning.
Don't worry about me. Now hurry back inside and rest. It's chilly out here. Don't catch a chill.
What do you think? Happy? Moved? Or... awestruck, maybe?
None of that. It was more like... How do I even put it...
So? Has the Nexus Fox Shadow truly returned to normal?
It has! Based on the data we pulled, Suhsin's influence has been completely neutralized!
{PlayerName}! You really kept your word! So you and Lady Hsin already dealt with Suhsin?
It's a long story. Tell me, has the Fox Shadow's behavior changed?
Yes! It's back to its original state!
That's not quite right. It isn't truly back to its "original state." Before, the Fox Shadow would either aid us on its own, or after we'd asked Lady Hsin for help.
But now that Lady Hsin is no longer within the Simulacrum Nexus, we can only reach it through the Shadow Binder. That's a world of difference.
True... And the Shadow Binder only mends the parts of the Fox Shadow that Suhsin corrupted. It's going to need some serious modifications from here on.
But at its core, the Fox Shadow is a creation of Fractal Proliferation. And Suhsin's power likely shares the same origin as Lady Hsin's. So perhaps all we need to do is adjust—
(I'd been worried the Fox Shadow might turn on them once Hsin was gone. Looks like I can finally put that fear to rest.)
Those "phantoms"... There have been more of them lately...
By "phantoms," do you mean the Mengzhou citizens scattered across the Simulacrum Nexus?
That's right. They're projections from Lady Hsin's memory data. I was completely baffled the first time I met them.
Back when we were studying the Civilization Capsule, it never crossed our minds that beings so vivid, so real, could exist within a civilization "blueprint."
But after Lady Hsin explained it, I understood. She believes the people of Mengzhou are part of its civilization too. That's why She did it.
What about you? Do you think a Civilization Capsule should include "phantoms" like them?
Haha, I can't speak for the other Sentinels. But if it's Lady Hsin's Civilization Capsule, then this is exactly how it should be.
All these "phantoms"... Can Lady Hsin really sustain every one of them?
All these "phantoms"... Can Lady Hsin really sustain every one of them?
What was that about Hsin?
{PlayerName}, surely you've noticed these "phantoms" come from different timelines, spanning centuries apart, yes?
I have. They're Hsin's memory projections, so it makes sense.
Exactly. But that means it costs Lady Hsin extra computational power to reunite people who could never otherwise have met, just to give them a chance to make up for their regrets.
That sounds just like Hsin. She can't bear to see people suffer. Is there some problem with that?
I'm just worried that the more "phantoms" there are, the heavier the burden on Her to keep them all here...
Don't worry. She knows Her own limits. If anything, take it as a good sign. We're only seeing this because Her condition is better than ever.
Ah, that's true. Hearing you say that puts my mind at ease. Guess I was worrying over nothing.
Look at this! My hands are trembling. The level of detail in Lady Hsin's simulation is really that precise.
Is this keyed to my frequency specifically, or is there some uniform logic behind it—
Stop right there. Your hands are shaking because you're exhausted. Quit analyzing and go take a break already.
Ugh, every time it comes to this, I always wonder why Lady Hsin even bothered to simulate a feeling like this. Rest, sleep, hunger… it's all just noise. It only gets in the way.
Look where we are. Inside the Civilization Capsule. Endless knowledge, the very  Sentinel technology we once only dreamed of now right in front of us. I don't have time to waste on—
I actually rather like it. Beyond just the knowledge, I get to enjoy the changing seasons and the beauty of this place.
And when I'm feeling worn out, I can find a good view and treat myself to some Moon Fox Rice Cakes. Doing that reminds me why we came here in the first place.
Why we came here? Wasn't it to study Sentinel technology and push civilization forward? I don't need reminding. I've never forgotten.

Yes, but I think the whole point of advancing civilization is to free people from suffering so they can experience things, enjoy them, and have the freedom to choose. If we lose sight of that along the way, what's the point?
Sigh... Maybe you've got a point. But as long as we've got someone like you around, that's enough for me. I'll just keep my head down and work!
Wow. You really are impossible.
Listen... my brain's too fried to work right now. How about you take me somewhere nice for some of those Moon Fox Rice Cakes?
So this grand cause, a century in the making, is finally drawing to a close?
{PlayerName}, thank you for your help. With Suhsin gone, the remolding has picked up pace. It won't be long now.
I accepted my fate the day I swore my oath. But I never expected that the one I'd find hardest to let go of... would be Lady Hsin.
That only sounds natural to me.
Haha, I suppose it would. You know Lady Hsin better than most. I imagine you understand exactly what I'm feeling right now.
The Sentinels we once knew cared for Solaris, without a doubt. But their compassion always felt distant. Noble, yet somehow beyond reach.

Lady Hsin, though... She'd come right up to us, praise our work, and gush about Her favorite stalls at the Waking Moon Festival. And when someone was lost to the anomalies... She'd cover her face and weep for them.
My resolve has never once faltered. Still, I count it as the fortune of three lifetimes—that the Sentinel I gave my oath to was Hsin the Moon Fox.
What do you think? Happy? Moved? Or... awestruck, maybe?
None of that. It was more like... How do I even put it...
Come on, it can't be that hard. You met Lady Hsin at the Waking Moon Festival. What else could you be but happy?
Of course I was happy. But there's more to it than just that.
It's just... that night, She moved through the crowd just like anyone else. But everyone's eyes were somehow drawn straight to Her.
They flocked to Her, but not me. I froze. Stood there like a stump, watching Her through all that noise and hustle.
She gave this little smile, and those gold-red eyes swept over the crowd. It was over in a heartbeat, but it felt like She looked at each one of us for an eternity...
I still can't put that feeling into words. All I know is that She seemed to see straight through me, and I knew I had to see Her again.
Next year... and every year after, you'll find me at the Waking Moon Festival.
Still no sign of Her this year. Could it be... Lady Hsin won't ever come again?
No... Next year, the year after, however long it takes, as long as I get to see Her one more time...
Granny! I gave the Gilded Ball to Lady Hsin! And She smiled back at me!
Does that mean She liked the gift?
Of course she did. Lady Hsin would never miss the heart behind it.
So, Yue, did you have a good time at the Waking Moon Festival?
I had the best time! Granny, you won't believe what happened! At first, Lady Hsin wasn't really Lady Hsin. Oh no, how do I explain this...
Take your time, dear. I'm listening.
Mm! Lady Hsin came with me to buy sugar paintings. Then we solved word riddles, took a boat ride, and watched the Loong dance! The performance was amazing!
And at the end, we set off fireworks. They were huge! Lady Hsin flew up into the sky, and bursts spread out behind Her, all bright and sparkly... It was so, so beautiful.
I really had the best time. I... I just wish you could've been there too.
Yue... all these years, you've been through so much.
Hm? Granny, don't say that! I've had a wonderful life!
The uncles and aunties in the village look after me like their own. And I met Lady Hsin! Remember the Gilded Ball you gave me? I got to give it to Her, just like you asked!
So don't worry about me. I'll grow up into a nice young lady, and I'll never forget the things you taught me.
That's my good girl. Now, tell me more about the Festival. What did you think when you first saw Her?
Hehe... Well, I thought She was a bit strange at first. When it happened, I was—
Wow! This Moon Lantern is so pretty! Big sister, can I take a look?
Of course. Here, come a little closer.
Hm... Oh! I saw what you wrote on it. Sounds like you've had a wonderful year!
I did. Lady Hsin will surely be glad to read it too. I just hope I get to see Her this year.
Hehe. I met Lady Hsin last year, you know!
Oh? We must've gone to the Festival at the same time. I met Lady Hsin, too.
You must've been thrilled to have gotten to see Her, hm?
Mm-hmm! But actually, I didn't even want to go at first. Granny had just passed, and it was her favorite holiday. I didn't want to go without her...
But Granny always said I had to hand the Gilded Ball to Lady Hsin myself. So I went.
And then...?
And then I really did meet Her! I gave Her the Gilded Ball, and She was so pleased. She even walked with me to see every bit of the Festival!
Well... have you ever heard the old legend?
"The Divine Fox descended from the moon. Where She walked, lanterns flickered to life. Crowds stirred. Festivity spread."
I know it! Granny told me. The rest goes like—"And She would weave through it all, take the hand of the lonely, and join the revelry."
Exactly. Oh, if your granny knew that you met Lady Hsin, and you delivered that Gilded Ball on her behalf... She'd be so proud.
Even the Shadow Binder is starting to lose its hold over... that great shadow.
If even the artifacts Lady Hsin made are failing, then Her condition must be...
Even the Shadow Binder is starting to lose its hold over... that great shadow.
If even the artifacts Lady Hsin made are failing, then Her condition must be...
Excuse me. Can I ask what you mean by "Her condition"?
{PlayerName}! Please, you may speak freely with us. Hmm... let me think how best to say it.
Let me. I'll be careful not to tip it off.

Here's how it is. Long ago, Lady Hsin used Her power of Fractal Proliferation to create the Nexus Fox Shadow. She entrusted it to watch over the entire Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou, and lend us aid whenever we called.
So, if the authority sustaining the Fox Shadow is starting to falter, then Lady Hsin... I'm sorry. That's all we can say.
Got it. Don't worry, Hsin and I will solve it together.
The Moon Fox Society. Hehe, what an amusing little group.
Arbiter! Where the Fox chases the Moon, all partings fade away!
Hm? Moon Fox Society?
That's the Moon Fox Society's code, isn't it? The next line goes: Where the Fox turns the wheel, fortune follows!
Just so. Seems the Arbiter is a member of the Moon Fox Society too.
Hm? What does that mean?
The Arbiter doesn't know? No initiations into the Moon Fox Society for you then, hehe.
If memory serves, they're very fond of you. Fanatical, almost. Wait, did you actually go to meet them?
I did. I knew of the Moon Fox Society even in my years bound to the Sanctum. I have long wished to meet them.
How did they take it? I wouldn't be surprised if they fainted on the spot and had to be carried off by Huaxu physicians.
At first, they stood quite frozen. It took two waves of my hand before they stirred from their daze.
Then came the bows, the reverent greetings, and, most tenderly, the concern over whether some ill fate had kept me from appearing all these years.
And in the end, they thanked me for guiding them through their lost days.
But Arbiter, I truly did nothing. And yet, now that I walk among them again, every gaze that falls upon me is filled with longing, with gratitude, with hope...
Are you still afraid you won't live up to it?
No. Not anymore. I am simply moved. A hundred years and more I have been unseen, and still, their love burns undimmed.
I am so glad... My charge is to guide the people of Mengzhou forward. But in this moment, I wish only to step into their midst. To laugh as they laugh, to feel their joy as if it were my own.
If I were to steal a little time for myself, would the Arbiter indulge me?
You wouldn't be stealing time. This is exactly what Mengzhou's Sentinel ought to be doing.
Hehe, as the Arbiter says. Perhaps this, too, is the Sentinel It hoped I would become.
Arbiter, did you catch the fire-breathers at the Waking Moon Festival? They were such fun.
I did. There were three of them.
I must have missed that.
Besides them, there were storytellers spinning tales at their stalls, acrobats juggling apples, and children performing the fish lantern dance.
Oh, and the Lantern Carriages, parading through the streets in rhythm with the fireworks. Such a lively, beautiful sight.
The Waking Moon Festival... what a joy.
Truly... what a year of blossoming bounty it has been.
Truly... what a year of blossoming bounty it has been.
Arbiter, came across a young girl's story just now. A full year of her life, written upon a Moon Lantern. It gladdened my heart to read.
Tell me about it.
In the warmth of spring, her father, who had spent years defending Xuanfang Hold, laid down his armor and returned home.
By the height of summer, her mother, long confined to her sickbed, rose again under their shared care.
Free of burden at last, she set out beneath autumn's golden light to pursue her dream of studying medicine.
And as the first snow of winter began to fall, she met the one her heart had been waiting for.
She sounds like a strong soul.
She is. Her father was gone for years, and she cared for her mother alone. That takes something rare.
Now that I can partake in the Festival again, I have seen so many lanterns bearing tidings of joy. It makes my heart feel full to bursting.
Would you hear a few more, Arbiter?
Of course. We have all the time in the world.
Wonderful! Then let me tell you of a boy who set out to find a Jadeplume Eagle...
Arbiter, come. Rest a while, and tell me of the days you have left behind.
Me? Hmm...
A flood of memories rises. You turn each one over in your mind, and after a pause, you begin to speak.
Joy and sorrow flicker across Hsin's face in turn, and every shift in Her expression makes the telling sweeter.
I may have gone on longer than I meant to. You did say the lanterns were only meant for happy stories, right?
Yes. The people of Mengzhou know I have a taste for life's pleasures and little fortunes, so they fill their lanterns with happy tidings, hoping to draw me near.
But what I truly want is for them to set their old griefs aside during the Festival. I hope that in their writing upon the lanterns, they learn to see their yesterdays with grace.
Arbiter, should hardship find you again one day, should grief return, I hope you will remember the moments that rang with laughter, and let them carry you forward.
So pray, continue, Arbiter. I would hear every word of it.
Yes... The likeness was uncanny. That's why I couldn't bring myself to do it.
Yes... The likeness was uncanny. That's why I couldn't bring myself to do it.
At the sound of footsteps, Suoming moves to put the Vermillion Locks away. When she sees that it is you, she stops.
Arbiter.
Talking to them?
Mm. I was telling them how Suhsin made a Ninth of its own.

Thank you, Lady Sentinel... for bending the rules for us.
The Waking Moon Festival in Xuanfang Hold is even more beautiful than I ever imagined.
Very well. If this is your wish, I will guard Xuanfang at all costs.
But... this land without you will forever be incomplete.
There are so many people waiting for you.
<color=XinyuehuSub>So many people... are waiting for me...</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>Since then, my remaining power could only sustain a brief manifestation once a year.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>I became the fabled Sentinel who appeared only during the grand festivals.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>When the morning bell rang, I was there.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>When the evening drum fell, I had to leave.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>But I wanted to be with them every day.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>To watch the dawn creep over their rooftops.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>To watch the chimney smoke melt into the twilight.</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>I wanted to breathe alongside this city, witnessing the flow of time with its people—</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>I thought our days would only grow brighter as Xuanfang neared completion... I had never imagined that those busy, precious days...</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>Would become the weight on the other side of the scales...</color>

Over the course of Xuanfang Hold's construction, Hsin overdraws Her computational power and grows weaker and weaker, until She can only manifest briefly at the Waking Moon Festival to share in the people's joy.

Slowly, she comes to love Xuanfang Hold and the people within it.
...Since the shift change two nights ago, Ovathrax launched a surprise raid at Desorock Highland, pushing straight toward the Clouded Cliffs.
It's broken our front lines and is nearing Yuan Fortress. Based on the Outriders' reports, it will reach the gates in thirty minutes.
The Threnodian clearly knew about Xuanfang Hold's construction... and planned this raid strategically. The Tacet Discords' assault is fierce. They've reached the mountain gates. We've already...
Lady Hsin, you...
Lady Hsin? Are you with me?
...Is there anyone left who can retreat?
A message came from the Central Plains. Only two words—
"No retreat."
We are holding here to establish a second line of defense. Ensure the civilians and critical mechanisms can evacuate.
Lady Hsin, as long as you're here, we still stand a chance. There will be a future for Xuanfang. Please—
You want me to leave and fight another day, don't you?
I understand your intent, but... my answer is the same as yours. The same two words.
No retreat.
Every moment I stay is one more life I can save.
My lady...
Enough. That is final. What is the status of the civilians?
Most have been evacuated, but some remain trapped near Yuan Fortress.
The perimeter is swarming with monsters summoned by Ovathrax. With our current forces... a full breakout is impossible.
But there are weak points. We can still carve a path through.
Prioritize the civilians. Notify all units...
In the name of Hsin the Moon Fox... In the name of the Sentinel of this land, follow my command. I will ensure everyone lives to see tomorrow.
...Understood! I will inform all units!
Wait. Before you go, tell me your name.
I am <ano=Feather-Brought>Yuxian</ano>. My mother told me a Xuanling Bird flew by when I was born, so she gave me this name. An interesting coincidence.
Yuxian... Good. I will remember it.
In this outbreak, the odds are slim. The least I can do is carry your names with me.
Remember: no matter what, I stand with you.
...Understood. Lady Hsin, it is time for me to return to the battlefield.
When you first arrived, that boy was barely seven. Now, he looks like a true "pillar" of the force.
And you, Little Fox? The enemy is at the gates, Jinzhou's affairs remain unresolved, and the true Sentinel is nowhere to be found.
The Threnodian knew our moves from the start. Waiting is death. Fighting is death. Even you, in your innocence, must see this is a stalemate.
Even if death awaits us either way, I cannot sit by.
Even if Ovathrax did not come today, it would eventually. We built Xuanfang to fight it.
All I can do is respond to the turn of battle and deploy Autopuppets as needed. At the very least, the civilians must be evacuated.
The battlefield shifts in a breath. Even with your Prism of Fate to see it all, relaying orders to every flank at once is impossible.
That's exactly why you are here, isn't it?
...Little Fox, have you thought this through?
Yes.
Then I will watch the battlefield for you and help you relay your commands.
Some of the civilians are still trapped... We must prioritize their safety.
I will buy them time.
These monsters have no mind of their own. They blindly pursue "people"...
No... Are they drawn to "battle"?
If that is the case...
Heh. So that is it.
Well done, Little Fox. The monsters are withdrawing.
Xuanling, tell everyone to stay hidden and move away from the Tacet Discords.
Good. Now the trapped citizens can escape.
How is our communication with Mingting? Any news?
The distress signal went out. But even at top speed, they are still five days away.
Five days... Too late.
The situation at the Gorges of Spirits is no better. We have to rely on these Autopuppets...
They keep coming...
Xuanling, tell everyone the civilians should be safe now. As for the rest... If it comes to it, save yourself first.
But...
I know. Xuanfang is the bridge between Mengzhou and the Jinzhou of the future. It cannot fall.
Yuan Fortress is the choke point. Once it falls, all of Xuanfang becomes as fragile as paper against the swarms.
I will find a way. If necessary... you know, I am also "Hsin the Moon Fox."
Still not enough... I have to find another way...
What... There are still people who haven't left?!
They refused to go.
The Warden Commander asked me to deliver this message.
...What did he say?
He said Yuxian passed on your orders. They each found stones and carved their names into them.
He has also organized the Artisans and Wardens to move to other sectors.
He said... as long as you are here, and as long as the Lexicon Axis you established stands, even on scorched earth, Xuanfang still has a future.
...Scorched earth?
No. Xuanling, tell him not to do anything stupid!
It is... too late.
You said you would stand with the people of Xuanfang, didn't you?
They, in turn, stand with the Sentinel who guards this land.
Little Fox, they all believe in you... We have no time for despair.
Most of the civilians were evacuated. Now we should help the Artisans still out there on the battlefield.
Before the explosion, Ruoyun relocated them all. I've marked their locations for you.
Mm.
Pull yourself together, Little Fox. Who are you pulling that long face for?
There were seven thousand souls here. You saved most of them amidst a relentless attack. What more do you want?
Wake up! You keep insisting you're also "Hsin the Moon Fox," remember?
What about the rest of the people? Let them die? They're all waiting for the Sentinel's commands.
I... I am sorry... I...
Tell me, what do you want, Little Fox?
I want them all to escape and live.
Xuanling, how much can you see?
Not much. The Threnodian's influence is too strong. Most of my companions can barely fly.
It's alright. Evacuate the front lines. Try to find survivors along the way and guide them to me.
We only need to hold until the last of them gather. Then I will create a new path for everyone to leave together.
Rest assured. The Artisans who failed to evacuate in time have already been guided to the vicinity of the Lexicon Axis.
Good. You and your companions can also follow them back now.
Little Fox, this may be the last you hear from me.
The Autopuppets cannot draw enough attention. Slow as Ovathrax is, it has already turned its eye toward Xuanfang.
There are soldiers still in the field. I will buy them time to reach the Axis.
...Xuanling.
Hush now, Little Fox. Even with the Sentinel here, the Xuanling are still the guardian spirits of this land.
Fate willing, we will meet again, Little Fox.
What remains is yours to carry, Sentinel—"Hsin."
Lady Hsin, can you hear me now?
The Wardens gave their lives for the Hold. The Xuanling Birds used their flesh to destroy the Fortress. We are at the brink, but this, right now, is also our opening.
The Tacet Discords are all gathered here. Now is the moment to finish them in one sweep.
Do you remember what you told us? If we merge with the Axis and surrender our own will, we can accelerate the Hold's completion.
You are... offering to become Celestials?
It is as we promised—those who build the Hold do not return.
Lady Hsin, this is the "price" we are willing to pay.
We know your concerns. One shouldn't be greedy, that is true. But... hehe, people like us are the greediest of all.
"Know the Way at dawn, die without regret at dusk."
But if I offer this body to my homeland at dawn, only to know the Way once more at dusk—what could be better?
This battle determines Xuanfang's fate. Lady Hsin, from now on, we are one with this Hold—
At this point, if I still hesitate, I might as well cast aside this human form.
In the end, I was never truly a Sentinel.
Perhaps it is this "heart" that kept me from ever becoming "Hsin the Moon Fox."

A vision simulated by the Heart Realm unfolds before you, and you watch the Fortress and Gorges War through Hsin's eyes.
 
Xuanfang Hold is nearly complete when Ovathrax's Tacet Discord hordes descend on Yuan Fortress. Warden Yuxian brings word that the front is in crisis. The Hsin of that day chose to save Xuanfang Hold and hold the line alongside soldiers and civilians alike.
 
Inside the memory, you walk in Hsin's shoes, making decisions and directing the Autopuppets to evacuate the people. In the Sanctum, She pushes Her power to its limit to accelerate the Hold's construction. Outside, the Wardens refuse to yield, and the Xuanling Birds dive into the city, giving their lives to slow the Tacet Discord advance. At the crisis point, the Court of Savantae's Artisans offer themselves to the Lexicon Axis early, becoming Celestials to bolster Hsin's strength. Grieving but resolute, Hsin gambles everything to force the Civilization Capsule to bring Xuanfang Hold to completion.
<color=XinyuehuSub>Using the Civilization Capsule to hasten Xuanfang Hold's completion...</color>
<color=XinyuehuSub>...There will be no turning back.</color>
What I just saw... That was everything you went through, wasn't it?
...You gave everything you had.
You've been in Xuanfang for a while now, Arbiter. Have you visited the Ministry of War?
There is a stone tablet there. Every single one of their names is engraved upon it.
I merely waved my hand. I merely offered a few words of judgment. They all acted on their own accord.
They walked away from the path I instructed and shielded a Hold that was never meant to exist. They gave their lives without a second thought.
In the end, all that remains of them is a name carved into cold stone. Faint. Hollow. One after another.
If no one speaks of them, they will be forgotten as if they never were.
They didn't throw themselves into the fire just to be remembered forever.
Hsin, you already did everything you could. They surely knew that. The circumstances...
The circumstances left no other choice, I know.
Speaking of which, I have been swept along by such circumstances many times.
Take past lantern festivals, for instance. In the form of a little fox, I could see their pain, but all I could offer were small gestures of comfort.
Sometimes I wondered... was my presence alone enough?
As long as I appeared before them, they felt safe. Happy. They believed they could endure the hard days.
But my reach was so limited, just as it is now. How is this any different from facing the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs back then?
I took a Capsule and ran. I ran and ran, searching for somewhere safe.
And they... they were all waiting for me to appear. Waiting for me to stand before them.
Round and round, and in the end, I am still that little fox.
But now, it should be different. After all, I have you with me now.
Thanks to you, I have seized more and more authority from Suhsin—from the "Sentinel's true will." The more I take, the more power I command.
The "Sentinel's true will"?
Yes, the Sentinel's underlying logic. Its true will.

The Sentinel believed that my remolding of the Civilization Capsule, my choice to preserve Xuanfang Hold, was a violation of the rules. A "loss of control." So it has been trying to reclaim the Hold to force it back onto its ordained path of ruin.
But thanks to you, I have gained the upper hand. The "anomalies" you fixed along the way have been strengthening my new authority.
—To break free from the Sentinel's will and forge new rules with my own hands.
With authority like that, I can finally do what the true "Hsin the Moon Fox" once could.
That girl carries my scent. It will make finding her easier.
Come, Arbiter. I know you still harbor many questions.
But right now, finding her and restoring Xuanfang Hold is what matters more, isn't it?
When all this is over, tell me what you're still holding back, okay?
Yes... I will when "all this" is over.

You open your eyes to find Hsin before you, Her spirits low. You raise what you just witnessed, but She deflects, brushing it off with a self-deprecating joke, calling herself a little fox swept along by events, changing the subject.
 
She tells you Suhsin embodies the "Sentinel's true will." In Suhsin's view, remolding the Civilization Capsule and preserving Xuanfang Hold broke the established order. Its goal has been to reclaim control and steer Xuanfang Hold back to its destined collapse. Every "anomaly" you repaired has strengthened Hsin's rewritten rules over Suhsin, allowing her now to wield the Moon Fox's power directly.

She opens the way into the Heartscape Labyrinth and asks you to join her to find Suoming and restore Xuanfang Hold. You can tell She's still hiding something. You make Her promise to tell you the rest once this is over.
The Waking Moon Festival... It's finally here...
I haven't been this happy in so long. When those Formrenders were around, I felt hollow, like my heart had been plucked out.
Those monsters are gone now! Things are going to get better from now on!
Lady Hsin... She'll come, right?
She loves a bustling festival too much to stay away.
See that "Moon Lantern" at the very top? Only She has the power to light it.
Come on! I found us the perfect spot to see the lanterns!
Mommy, look! A little fox!
A fox? Where did you see it?
Don't rush, sweetheart, you'll bump into someone!
The lanterns are so beautiful...
What wish are you going to write on yours?
Just health, safety, and smooth days ahead for my family.
<color=XinyuehuSub>Run, Hsin... Run faster. Everyone... is waiting for this!</color>
May all beings rejoice... the Moon and lanterns ever bright...
Does this sight bring you any comfort, old friend?
Forgive me. Your frequency was fading too quickly, and all I could gather from the people's longings was this single thread. If It were here... It would have done better.
Look, the Waking Moon lanterns are lit once more. Let us linger in this view a little longer.
From now on, everything will be well.

In the fox's body, you leap for the moon in the sky and restore its light. The lanterns blaze bright as day, and the Waking Moon Festival becomes at last what it was always meant to be.

Off in a quiet corner, Hsin's phantom stands gazing down at the lights, a Rafter Kite perched on her fingertip. Her face is soft, as if catching up with an old friend.
Look! That door over there! Isn't that where we came from?
Arbiter.
Hsin the Moon Fox?
Just "Hsin" will do.
Thanks to you, the Heart of Flames has recovered. I've reclaimed enough authority to meet you like this.
Before this, I had no way to speak with you directly. I could only guide you here. It must be a long journey for you, Arbiter. Would you... like to rest? Have some pastries?
(Shake your head.)
(Take the rice cakes.)
...Let's skip the pleasantries.
Hsin, I have so much to ask you.
You've been missing for some time. Where were you? What happened to you?
What you saw before was merely a fractured strand of myself. My true form still sleeps deep within the Simulacrum Nexus.
I thought I could spare the strength to find you. But anomalies kept appearing. I've had to pour everything into repairs. I'm spread... terribly thin.
Even now, I can only speak to you in this unstable form.
From what I gathered, Muyu's corrupted Reverberations have all been purged. Xuanfang Hold should be safe now.
What is truly binding you, Hsin?
Ha. Nothing escapes you.
Is it the Fox Shadow?
It has your face. Your frequency. But every Celestial I met spoke of it with dread. I think they were under some kind of restriction.
The Heart Realm anomalies, the canceled Waking Moon Festival... Is the Fox Shadow behind it all?
It took Suoming too. Do you know where she is now?
Mm... that is a lot of questions at once...
That "Nexus Fox Shadow," let's call it "Suhsin." It began to break free of my control after I decided to remold the Civilization Capsule. Since then, it has been spreading through the Nexus.

Suhsin seeks to devour all "Sentinel Hsin the Moon Fox" data to stabilize its own existence. It's been fighting me for control over Xuanfang Hold. In our struggle, I took my eyes off the Hold. A part of the Sanctum collapsed because of it.
As for that girl with the umbrella, she deliberately released the Moon Fox frequency in her token to lure Suhsin into taking her. Reaching Suhsin was her goal all along.
But the Heart Realm she's in now... is currently beyond my reach.
Hm... but there is one simple way to make Suhsin obey your every command.
What is it?
Use the power within the Prism of Fate to overwrite my personality data and reset all clearances. Since Suhsin shares my source code, it will revert to its initial state.
And what would happen to you?
Well, I'd lose my sense of self and exist solely as the core to keep Xuanfang Hold running, wouldn't I?
I won't allow that to happen.
Aw, not that frown, Arbiter. I was only joking.
Why was Suhsin able to drive you into such a corner? What could override a Sentinel's authority?

Suhsin's clearance... comes from the Civilization Capsule's base code. Its core logic dictates that once Xuanfang Hold fulfills its mission, it must be destroyed. To keep the Hold, I had no choice but to overwrite it with new logic.
So that's the reason you remolded the Capsule?
...Yes.
Shh. Tread lightly. We wouldn't want a giant hand to appear and snatch us both away!
Then let me ask you this: are the things shown in the Heart Realms your memories?
...They are.
You made Xuanfang's very first Rafter Kite, didn't you? Then who is the "It" you mentioned to that Rafter Kite?
That is—
Ah... my time in human form is up.
Tell me, what do you need me to do now?
Arbiter, please continue through the Heart Realms. Venture deep into the Simulacrum Nexus to fix the anomalies. I will be waiting at the end of the next Realm.
What I am forbidden to say aloud is hidden within those fragments of the past. Once you have witnessed everything, you will understand why I brought you here.
...Forgive me.
The Providence Lock didn't react. Guess Hsin was telling the truth.
What's that over there...?

You step back through the door into your own body, and Hsin the Moon Fox is waiting for you in the flesh. She tells you to call Her "Hsin" and thanks you for clearing the anomaly in the Heart of Flames—the only reason this meeting is possible at all.
 
You press Her with your many questions. She admits that Her true self has been trapped deep inside the Simulacrum Nexus all along, bound by the entity behind the Nexus Fox Shadow, the one She calls "Suhsin." Suhsin emerged from the Civilization Capsule's base code, and its core logic dictates that Xuanfang Hold be destroyed once its mission is complete. Hsin overwrote that logic with Her own in order to keep Xuanfang Hold standing. Suhsin has been fighting back ever since, tearing loose and seeding anomalies across the Nexus while Hsin struggles to maintain control of the Hold.

As for Suoming, she let Suhsin take her on purpose, for reasons of her own. The Heart Realm she now occupies lies under Suhsin's control, beyond Hsin's reach.

Hsin asks you to press deeper into the Simulacrum Nexus and repair the remaining Heart Realms. Everything the restrictions keep Her from saying is buried in the memories those Heart Realms hold.
An invitation letter. No trace of the sender can be found on the envelope.
Here's my plan. We let a Formrender break the restriction on the Lantern Pavilion for us, lead it off somewhere, and slip in while it's distracted.
Are you out of your mind?!
And then, ten thousand Autopuppets descended from the sky like a blessing. Every heart lifted, and the clouds finally broke, and the moon shone through...
Whoa... And then? What happened to the city?
Child, we're standing in it.
We only wanted a Waking Moon Festival. What's so wrong with that?
Maybe it's the Sentinel. She isn't the same anymore...
Nonsense! I'll tell you what it is. Those monsters crawled up from who knows where, and they can't stand to see anyone happy. That's why they wreck everything!
The Waking Moon Festival is almost here... I'll wait for him here. He'd like that, wouldn't he?
Grandma... it's been decades. Grandpa isn't coming back...

To my wife, Mingxi,

I hope this letter finds you well. Your note and the dried fruit reached me safely, and I am in good health. There is no need to worry about me. Not a single piece was crushed on the way, and I confess I could not bring myself to share any with my colleagues; I ate them all myself. Each one was wonderfully sweet, and I was quite content. I only hope that next time you might spare a few more words for me.

Matters at the Ministry have kept me busy of late, so this reply comes later than it should. Forgive me. I have picked out a hairpin for you, one of the styles now fashionable in the city, in a pattern I know you like. As for the reassignment, it is still under discussion, and my posting has not been decided. I mention it only so that it will not sit on your mind later.

By the time this reaches you, autumn will likely have set in. Remember to dress warmly in the mornings and evenings. Do not give all your attention to the children. Perhaps you might treat yourself to a few new garments? Counting the days, I may be able to take leave around the time of the Waking Moon Festival. If the leave is granted, I will be home before dusk, and we will go to see the lanterns together.

There is more in my heart than this page can hold. Take good care of yourself.

Yours,
Guilan
The lanterns are lit, the feast is laid out... So this is the Waking Moon Festival Mommy always talked about...
Where do you want to go first?
I want to see the fox chasing the moon!
That... is that even a real thing?
A carefully made Moon Lantern. The first lantern She ever received in the Land of Xuanfang, and Her first wish.
A little warmth from mortal hands, and a lost "heart" found its light.
(So this is the "Heart Realm" the Celestials talked about, deep in the Sanctum...)
(Suoming didn't seem like she'd lost control. She let herself be taken on purpose.)
(My Terminal... Signal's down, just as I thought. At least she and I agree on the priority. Finding the real Hsin the Moon Fox.)
...Is that the same fox from earlier?
Ooh, its frequency... it smells similar to the one in the Prism of Fate!
Are you... "Hsin's" messenger?
Why doesn't the Moon Fox just come to you Herself? I mean, She created this whole place. What could possibly trap Her?
I'm afraid it's not that simple.
Ugh, why's it always such a mess... Oh! Come to think of it, that thing the umbrella girl was holding had Hsin's frequency in it, too. Only kinda different...
Different how...?
Umm, like... plain rice versus egg fried rice? Both rice, sure, but the girl's had a lot more flavor... Hey! Hey! Are you ever gonna stop petting that fox?!
What, now it's taking our stuff—!
...Is it leading me through there?
...Abby?
You... wha... how'd you turn into that?
...What the heck is going on here?!
The Celestial said the Sanctum shifts with Hsin the Moon Fox's heart, but that every change follows a rule. Could this... be one of those rules at work?
What kind of rule swaps people and foxes around...? So you think She's behind this?
If some restrictions kept me from acting freely, I'd find another way to get my message across, too.
I sensed nothing hostile from that fox. Maybe... I can only move through this Heart Realm in this form?
A thousand lanterns line up like clouds in motion, their songs and steps wake the sleeping stars.
If mortal smiles might yet be born of this, what harm to walk by moon and lantern light?
...Light the lanterns, gather the guests... Invite the Moon... All beings... rejoice...
...Was that Hsin?
"Light the lanterns, gather the guests"... Every lantern here is unlit.
Better keep moving for now.

The little fox lets you pet it without protest. Abby notes that its frequency closely resembles the one in the Prism of Fate, though not quite the same as the Hsin frequency within Suoming's Vermillion Lock. Then, without warning, the fox snatches the Prism of Fate from your hands and darts toward a nearby door.
 
You chase it through, only to find that you and the fox have swapped bodies. Hsin's voice drifts from nowhere: "Light the lanterns, gather the guests. Invite the Moon." You need the Prism back, so you listen to the voice and step forward.
You feeling okay in there?
I'm fine. Just... can't really swing a sword like this.
Hehe, relax. I've got your back!
That frequency just now, it smells just like that big shadow outside!
Maybe the anomaly here is connected to whatever's restricting Hsin's authority.
Mmh... feels like something's watching us. Got this gross, squeezy feeling that won't go away.
Yeah. I've felt it too, ever since I took this form.
Unease, dread, and a suffocating sense of confinement hang over the heart like a shadow.
It went that way.
It returned the Prism of Fate... It was only showing me the way all along.
Hsin... what is it you truly want me to do?
Have you lost your mind? Out here lighting lanterns alone, at a time like this!
You know full well lantern light draws the Formrenders. Last time, you almost got...
I've been watching. They've gone quiet for now. Let me give it another go.
Wh-what's that?
Forget the lantern. Run!
("Light the lanterns, gather the guests"... Am I supposed to light these?)
(I'll pick up that Moon Lantern first.)
Was that the Prism of Fate resonating?
Hehe, this gizmo Hsin gave you is pretty handy, huh!

...It has been ██ days since the Formrenders first appeared, and at last we have found a way to relight the Moon Lanterns.

Those faint glimmers scattered through the alleys—Luobin calls them <color=Highlight>Nightlight Tokens</color>—carry some very peculiar frequency. <color=Highlight>Burn them in the Moon Lanterns, and the darkness gives way.</color> They suppress the Formrenders too: the brighter the flame, the heavier their limbs, the slower their approach. But each lantern lit also draws their attention, so we must move with care.

Where the glimmers come from, none of us knows. Faint as they are, one always rekindles somewhere just as the oil runs dry and the wick burns out. Whatever the truth of it, so long as we have the Nightlight Tokens, there is still hope. Jianwei believes it is a blessing bestowed by the Sentinel... But if it truly is a blessing, why has She never shown Herself?

...Last night I heard the wind sweep down the corridor, and in my terror I snatched up a weapon and rushed outside, only to frighten my neighbors half to death. Then I remembered the Fortress and Gorges War ended long ago. My memory really has been failing me of late. Best to write it all down.

...Those who have seen it call it the Formrender. Blue of face, long of fang, it wears the shape of an Autopuppet, yet the air about it is foul. Its voice grates like a rusted blade scraping bone, and a red light sits in its eyes. It keeps to dark places, and loathes above all the joys of mortal men. At the sight of them it wakes to wrath, and in its wrath it devours that light.
A note scrawled in a hurry.

"...Tried to light a lantern. A Formrender was on me within seconds. Chased me to the end of the alley—I only escaped by luck. The new lantern shattered too... One Moon Lantern isn't enough. They have to go up together, many at once."
"Beware the paintings. If you see a Formrender, run. Don't stop."
Three more gone just like that. Now Nightlight Tokens are running low. This year's Waking Moon Festival... I doubt we can hold it.
Ugh. All I want is to light one lantern. Say a prayer for peace. When did that get so hard?
And these Formrenders, heaven knows where those monsters came from. Not Autopuppets, not Tacet Discords... Just show up and snuff out any lantern they see, like they're possessed.
One nearly got that boy Luobin last time...
What else can we do? We've tried everything. These things won't leave. All of us are on edge.
Say... if we can't hold the festival, do you think Lady Hsin will still come?
...Has She given up on us?
Don't say such things. Why else would the Sentinel have built the Hold?
Let's lay low for now. Wait it out.
Haah, thought we'd finally catch a break after the Fortress and Gorges War.
Hm... how long ago was that again? Funny, I can't seem to remember...

From the residents, you gather that this Heart Realm reflects Xuanfang Hold in the years after the Fortress and Gorges War. The people here have given up on holding the Waking Moon Festival. Monsters called Formrenders prowl the streets, extinguishing every lit lantern and attacking anyone who dares try.
Weird. What kind of monster exists just to snuff out lanterns?
The Waking Moon Festival is an age-old tradition in the Land of Xuanfang, but here they're saying it can't be held this year.
What if the way to reach Hsin in this Heart Realm is to make the festival happen first?
Let's try lighting up those lanterns.
Whoa, whoa! That thing just crawled right out of the painting... and now it's coming for us!
